REPRODUCTIVE__Testis (seminiferous tubul:
Overview

The testis makes sperm in seminiferous tubules and testosterone in the interstitium. A capsule (tunica albuginea) divides it into lobules of tubules.

🔬 Image slot — seminiferous tubule with spermatogenic cells + Sertoli cells, and interstitial Leydig cells
The Cells ⭐
CellLocationRole
Spermatogenic cellsTubule wall (basal → luminal maturation)Spermatogonia → spermatocytes → spermatids → spermatozoa
Sertoli cellsTall, span the tubule wallSupport/nurse sperm; tight junctions form the blood–testis barrier; secrete inhibin & androgen-binding protein; respond to FSH
Leydig (interstitial) cellsBetween tubulesSecrete testosterone in response to LH
Clinical / Pathological Correlate
Cryptorchidism
Undescended testis → impaired spermatogenesis & ↑cancer risk.
Testicular tumours
Germ-cell tumours (seminoma commonest); Leydig/Sertoli-cell tumours (hormonal).
Infertility
Sertoli-cell-only syndrome; disrupted blood–testis barrier → anti-sperm antibodies.
⭐ Exam Pearls
  • Sperm made in seminiferous tubules; testosterone in Leydig cells (interstitium).
  • Sertoli cells = FSH, support, blood–testis barrier, inhibin; Leydig cells = LH, testosterone.
  • Maturation goes basal → luminal; commonest testicular cancer = seminoma.
REPRODUCTIVE__Ovary (follicles, corpus l:
Overview

The ovary houses follicles at various stages in its cortex; each cycle a follicle matures, ovulates, and becomes a corpus luteum (then a corpus albicans).

🔬 Image slot — ovarian cortex with primordial, primary and Graafian follicles + a corpus luteum
Follicle Stages ⭐
StageFeatures
PrimordialOocyte + single flat granulosa layer
PrimaryCuboidal granulosa; zona pellucida appears
Secondary (antral)Fluid-filled antrum; theca interna (androgens) + externa
Graafian (mature)Large antrum; oocyte on the cumulus oophorus; ovulates
After ovulation: corpus luteum (granulosa + theca lutein cells secrete progesterone) → if no pregnancy, regresses to a scar, the corpus albicans.
Clinical / Pathological Correlate
PCOS
Multiple arrested follicles ('string of pearls'); anovulation.
Ovarian cysts / tumours
Functional cysts; teratoma (germ cell), serous/mucinous (epithelial), granulosa-cell (oestrogen).
⭐ Exam Pearls
  • Follicle order: primordial → primary (zona pellucida) → secondary/antral → Graafian.
  • Theca interna → androgens; granulosa → oestrogen (FSH); corpus luteum → progesterone.
  • Post-ovulation: corpus luteum → corpus albicans (white scar).
  • PCOS = 'string of pearls' arrested follicles.
REPRODUCTIVE__Uterus (endometrium — mens:
Overview — The Uterine Wall

Three layers: endometrium (mucosa that cycles), myometrium (thick smooth muscle) and perimetrium (serosa). The endometrium has a functional layer (shed each period) and a basal layer (regenerates it).

🔬 Image slot — endometrium in proliferative vs secretory phase (straight vs coiled glands)
The Menstrual Cycle on the Slide ⭐
PhaseHormoneEndometrium
Menstrual (d1–4)↓ hormonesFunctional layer sheds
Proliferative (d5–14)OestrogenRegrows; straight tubular glands, mitoses
Secretory (d15–28)Progesterone (corpus luteum)Coiled 'saw-tooth' glands, glycogen-rich secretion, spiral arteries, oedema
Progesterone withdrawal (no pregnancy) → spiral-artery constriction → ischaemia → menstruation.
Clinical / Pathological Correlate
Endometrial hyperplasia/carcinoma
Unopposed oestrogen → hyperplasia → adenocarcinoma (postmenopausal bleeding).
Endometriosis / adenomyosis
Endometrial tissue outside the cavity (endometriosis) or within the myometrium (adenomyosis).
Leiomyoma (fibroid)
Benign myometrial smooth-muscle tumour.
⭐ Exam Pearls
  • Endometrium: functional layer sheds; basal layer regenerates.
  • Proliferative (oestrogen) = straight glands; secretory (progesterone) = coiled saw-tooth glands + glycogen.
  • Progesterone withdrawal → spiral-artery ischaemia → menses.
  • Unopposed oestrogen → hyperplasia/carcinoma; fibroid = myometrial leiomyoma.
REPRODUCTIVE__Prostate Gland:
Overview

The prostate is a fibromuscular gland surrounding the urethra that adds fluid to semen. It is a set of tubuloalveolar glands in a prominent fibromuscular stroma.

🔬 Image slot — prostate glands in fibromuscular stroma with a corpus amylaceum
  • Glands lined by two layers: secretory (tall columnar) + basal cells — loss of the basal layer signals malignancy
  • Corpora amylacea = concentric eosinophilic concretions in the lumina (increase with age)
  • Zones: peripheral (cancer), transitional (BPH, around the urethra), central
Clinical / Pathological Correlate
Benign prostatic hyperplasia
Transitional zone nodular hyperplasia → urinary obstruction.
Prostate adenocarcinoma
Peripheral zone; small crowded glands with loss of the basal cell layer; graded by Gleason score; ↑PSA.
⭐ Exam Pearls
  • Prostate = tubuloalveolar glands (two cell layers) in fibromuscular stroma.
  • Corpora amylacea = luminal concretions (age).
  • BPH = transitional zone; cancer = peripheral zone + loss of basal cells (Gleason, PSA).
REPRODUCTIVE__Fallopian Tube:
Overview

The uterine (fallopian) tube captures the ovum and is the site of fertilisation, then transports the embryo to the uterus.

🔬 Image slot — fallopian tube mucosa with branching folds, ciliated + peg cells
  • Highly folded (plicated) mucosa lined by simple columnar epithelium with two cell types:
  • Ciliated cells — waft the ovum/embryo toward the uterus
  • Peg (secretory) cells — nourish the ovum & capacitate sperm
  • Smooth-muscle wall provides peristalsis; regions: infundibulum (fimbriae) → ampulla (fertilisation) → isthmus → intramural
Clinical / Pathological Correlate
Ectopic pregnancy
Most implant in the ampulla; risk of rupture & haemorrhage (PID/scarring predisposes).
Salpingitis / PID
Infection → scarring → infertility & ectopic risk.
⭐ Exam Pearls
  • Fallopian tube = folded simple columnar epithelium: ciliated cells (transport) + peg/secretory cells (nourish).
  • Fertilisation occurs in the ampulla — also the commonest site of ectopic pregnancy.
  • PID/salpingitis → scarring → infertility & ectopic risk.
REPRODUCTIVE__Cervix:
Overview — A Junction of Two Epithelia ⭐

The cervix links uterus and vagina; the key histological point is the transformation zone where two epithelia meet.

🔬 Image slot — cervical squamocolumnar junction / transformation zone
RegionEpithelium
Ectocervix (vaginal)Non-keratinised stratified squamous
Endocervix (canal)Simple columnar mucus-secreting; branching glands
Transformation zone (SCJ)Where squamous meets columnar — site of metaplasia & where dysplasia/cancer arises
Nabothian cysts = mucus-filled endocervical glands blocked by overlying squamous metaplasia (benign).
Clinical / Pathological Correlate
HPV & CIN
High-risk HPV (16/18) at the transformation zone → koilocytes → CIN (dysplasia) → squamous cell carcinoma.
Cervical screening
Smear samples the transformation zone (HPV test + cytology).
⭐ Exam Pearls
  • Ectocervix = stratified squamous; endocervix = simple columnar; they meet at the squamocolumnar junction / transformation zone.
  • The transformation zone is where metaplasia, HPV-driven dysplasia (CIN) and cervical cancer arise — and what a smear samples.
  • Koilocytes = HPV cytopathic effect; Nabothian cysts = benign blocked glands.
REPRODUCTIVE__Placenta:
Overview — The Materno-Fetal Interface

The placenta exchanges gases, nutrients and waste between mother and fetus across chorionic villi bathed in maternal blood.

🔬 Image slot — placental chorionic villi with syncytiotrophoblast, cytotrophoblast and fetal vessels
  • Chorionic villi = fetal fingers projecting into maternal blood (the intervillous space)
  • Villus surface: outer syncytiotrophoblast (multinucleate; hormone synthesis & exchange) over inner cytotrophoblast (stem cells, prominent early)
  • Villus core: fetal capillaries + connective tissue (with Hofbauer cells = fetal macrophages)
  • Syncytiotrophoblast secretes hCG, hPL, oestrogen, progesterone
Clinical / Pathological Correlate
Hydatidiform mole
Swollen (hydropic) villi + trophoblast proliferation; very high hCG.
Choriocarcinoma
Malignant trophoblast; hCG-secreting; haematogenous spread.
Pre-eclampsia
Defective trophoblast invasion of spiral arteries → placental ischaemia.
⭐ Exam Pearls
  • Exchange unit = chorionic villus: syncytiotrophoblast (outer) over cytotrophoblast (inner), fetal vessels in the core.
  • Syncytiotrophoblast makes hCG, hPL, oestrogen, progesterone.
  • Hofbauer cells = fetal macrophages in the villus.
  • Molar pregnancy = hydropic villi + trophoblast proliferation (high hCG); can → choriocarcinoma.
REPRODUCTIVE__Breast (resting & lactatin:
Overview

The breast is a modified tubuloalveolar (apocrine) gland arranged in lobules of ducts and (in lactation) alveoli, set in fat and fibrous stroma.

🔬 Image slot — resting breast (mostly stroma/ducts) vs lactating breast (secretory alveoli)
Resting (non-lactating)
  • Mostly fibrofatty stroma with scattered ducts; few/no alveoli; the terminal duct lobular unit (TDLU) is where most disease arises
Lactating
  • Abundant secretory alveoli full of milk; little stroma; milk made by merocrine (protein) + apocrine (fat) secretion
Ducts/alveoli have a two-layer lining: luminal epithelial cells + outer myoepithelial cells (contract under oxytocin to eject milk).
Clinical / Pathological Correlate
Fibroadenoma
Commonest benign tumour (young women); mobile 'breast mouse'.
Carcinoma
Arises in the TDLU; ductal/lobular; loss of myoepithelial layer = invasion; ER/PR/HER2 typing.
Fibrocystic change
Cysts, fibrosis, adenosis — commonest benign breast condition.
⭐ Exam Pearls
  • Resting breast = mostly stroma/ducts; lactating = secretory alveoli (milk via merocrine + apocrine).
  • Two-layer lining: epithelial + myoepithelial (oxytocin → milk ejection); loss of the myoepithelial layer signals invasion.
  • Most breast disease (incl. carcinoma) arises in the terminal duct lobular unit (TDLU).
  • Fibroadenoma = commonest benign tumour; carcinomas typed by ER/PR/HER2.
